title: Highest-Protein Cheeses: Ranking Per 100 Grams

seo.title: Highest-Protein Cheeses per 100 Grams
seo.meta_description: Compare Parmesan, Gruyère, cheddar, mozzarella and cottage cheese by protein, and see why aging and water content change the ranking.

excerpt: Hard aged cheeses lead protein-per-100-gram rankings because they contain less water. Parmesan can approach 36 grams per 100 grams, but serving size, fat, sodium and calories change the practical comparison.
content_html:
Aged cheese becomes nutritionally concentrated as moisture is lost. That is why Parmesan can contain more protein per 100 grams than many meats—even though people eat much smaller portions.

Representative ranking

CheeseApprox. protein/100 g
Parmesan35–36 g
Other hard grating cheeses32–35 g
Gruyère29–30 g
Swiss-type cheese26–28 g
Cheddar24–25 g
Low-moisture mozzarella22–25 g
Fresh mozzarella16–20 g
Cottage cheese11–13 g

Why Parmesan ranks so high

Hard aging removes water, concentrating protein along with fat, calcium and sodium. A one-ounce serving provides roughly 10 grams of protein—not the 36 grams implied by a 100-gram column.

Fresh versus aged cheese

Fresh cheeses contain more water, so protein per 100 g is lower. That does not make them nutritionally weak. Cottage cheese, for example, is often eaten in a half-cup or one-cup serving and can deliver a large amount of protein with fewer calories than an equal weight of hard cheese.

Protein and fat rise together in many cheeses

Parmesan and cheddar are concentrated sources of both. If your priority is maximum protein per calorie, low-fat cottage cheese or high-protein yogurt may outperform a hard cheese.

Mozzarella is not one product

Fresh mozzarella holds much more water than low-moisture mozzarella used on pizza. Removing moisture raises protein, fat and calories per 100 grams.

Sodium deserves equal attention

Cheese can be a major sodium source. Hard and brined cheeses vary widely. A high protein number should therefore be interpreted alongside serving size and sodium on the label.

Serving-size comparison

CheeseServingApprox. protein
Parmesan30 g10–11 g
Cheddar30 g7–8 g
Low-moisture mozzarella30 g7 g
Cottage cheese150 g17–20 g

Frequently asked questions

Which cheese has the most protein?

Parmesan and similar hard aged cheeses are among the most concentrated at roughly 33–36 g per 100 g.

Why does aged cheese have more protein?

It contains less water, so nutrients are concentrated by weight.

Is cottage cheese lower in protein?

Per 100 g, yes, but typical servings are larger and can provide more total protein with fewer calories than a large hard-cheese portion.

faq.question: Which cheese is highest in protein?
faq.answer: Parmesan and other hard aged cheeses can provide roughly 33–36 g per 100 g.

faq.question: Why is aged cheese so protein-dense?
faq.answer: Moisture loss during production and aging concentrates protein per unit of weight.

faq.question: Does highest protein mean leanest cheese?
faq.answer: No. Hard cheeses often concentrate fat and calories too.
